exercise.name: 2 to 1 Jump Box

reference.title: 2 to 1 Jump Box (male)
reference.note: Used only to identify the movement. This rig, artwork and animation are original. Box height is not given by the reference; the animation uses a 30 cm box.

exercise.type: Plyometric (lower-body power and single-leg landing control)
equipment: Plyo box, 30 cm (a soft-sided foam box is the safer choice)
exercise.laterality: Bilateral takeoff, unilateral landing (alternate landing legs)

muscleNotes.quads_r: Landing leg: extends the knee at takeoff, then brakes the knee bend on the catch. Single-leg jump landings showed higher early quadriceps activity than drop landings.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Drives the two-foot takeoff with the landing leg.
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extension at takeoff and controls the hip hinge on the catch.
muscleNotes.calves_r: Ankle push-off at takeoff and the first part of the catch. (Tibialis anterior and peroneus longus also steady the landing ankle; the rig has no region for them.)
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Hip extension at takeoff and support for the knee on landing.
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip at takeoff.
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Adductor magnus helps extend the hip at takeoff.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Forward arm swing that adds to the takeoff, then holds the arms forward for balance.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Forward arm swing that adds to the takeoff, then holds the arms forward for balance.
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Holds the free (left) leg up off the box, behind and below the body, through the stick.
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Keeps the pelvis level over the single foot and resists the knee caving in.
muscleNotes.core: Braces the trunk through the catch and the stick.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Keeps the trunk steady over one foot.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Keeps the trunk steady over one foot.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Holds the chest up over the knee in the hinge.
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Holds the chest up over the knee in the hinge.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in while standing tall and during the dip; breathe out sharply on the takeoff; hold a short brace through the catch and the stick; breathe out as you stand up on the box; breathe normally while stepping down and resetting.
breathing.cadence: About 0.5 s dip, a fast takeoff, about 1 to 2 s stick on the box, then a slow step down and a 2 to 3 s reset

prescription.reps: 3 to 5 per landing leg (switch landing legs each set)
prescription.rest: About 60 to 90 s between sets (full recovery); every rep at full quality
prescription.frequency: 2 to 3 sessions per week, 48 to 72 h between plyometric sessions
prescription.boxHeight: Start low (about 15 to 30 cm); raise it only while landings stay quiet and the knee stays aligned
prescription.programLength: Basic plyometric blocks run about 4 to 6 weeks
prescription.tempo: Fast dip and takeoff, 1 to 2 s stick, slow step down, 2 to 3 s reset

cues.text: Stand tall facing the box, a short step away, feet hip-width.
Hips back into a quarter squat, arms swing back.
Drive both feet through the floor and swing the arms up.
Land softly on one foot, knee bent over your toes, hips back.
Knee tracks over the second toe. Freeze for two counts, free leg off the box.
Stand tall on the box, then step down. Don't jump down.
Reset fully before the next rep. Switch landing legs each set.

mistakes.mistake: Knee caves inward on the landing leg
mistakes.fix: Lower the box. Cue "knee over second toe" and "spread the floor". Build glute med strength with single-leg squats.
Cue "land quietly"; bend the knee and hip on contact. A soft landing lowered peak force in studies.

mistakes.mistake: Box too high: the athlete tucks the knees and lands in a deep squat
mistakes.fix: Pick a height where the landing knee bend stays near about 45 to 50 degrees. Height is not the goal.

mistakes.mistake: Hips stay forward and the trunk falls back on landing
mistakes.fix: Cue "hips back, chest over knee", then hinge.

mistakes.mistake: Free leg touches down or the athlete hops to recover balance
mistakes.fix: Lower the box, slow the stick, hold the landing two counts before standing.

mistakes.mistake: Jumping back down off the box
mistakes.fix: Step down every rep; a jump down adds an unplanned drop landing.
Fully reset between reps and stop the set when landings get louder or the knee drifts.

kinematics.norm: Quarter-to-half squat. A self-selected dip averaged ≈0.36 m centre-of-mass drop in a maximal vertical jump; a shallower dip cut jump height ≈8% and a deeper one added nothing. No verified knee angle for a box-jump dip.
The reference shows a quarter squat; a maximal countermovement jump self-selects ≈36 cm centre-of-mass drop.

kinematics.measure: Knee flexion at initial contact (landing leg)
kinematics.norm: ≈9–13° in single-leg landings and hops (≈9–10° after a forward jump from a 30 cm box); double-leg landings touch down at ≈16–18°.
≈46° natural and ≈50° soft single-leg landing; contact-to-peak range ≈40–46°. Authoring target 45–50°.

kinematics.measure: Hip flexion on the catch (landing leg)
kinematics.norm: ≈26–27° in a single-leg lateral jump-landing (thin, indirect data). Authoring target: a visible hip hinge of ≈30–45°.

kinematics.setup: Knee over the second and third toes
kinematics.peak: No inward collapse: the knee stays over the foot
kinematics.norm: 2D valgus in a step landing ≈1–9° (men) and ≈5–12° (women); single-leg drop-jump FPPA ≈12° in active men. Between-day change ≈7.5–9°, so small differences mean little.
Animation choice, not a research norm: a 30 cm box, landing foot near the middle of the box top. Research guidance is to start low (≈15–30 cm) and raise the box only while landings stay quiet.

cautions: Plyometrics are not for unconditioned athletes, unyielding surfaces, a history of stress-related injury, acute or sub-acute sprains, acute inflammation, post-operative status or joint instability.
Build adequate strength, near-full range of motion, balance and body control before plyometric work.
After ACL reconstruction or with knee pain, clear the drill with a clinician first; one-leg landing drills belong to the later, return-to-sport stages of rehab.
Pregnancy, osteoporosis or a balance disorder: skip it or substitute a low-impact option.
Use a stable, non-slip box on a non-slip floor; a soft-sided box reduces shin-scrape risk on a missed jump.
modify: Lower the box (or use a soft box) until landings are quiet and the knee stays over the toes.
Hold every landing two counts before standing; stop the set when landings get louder or the knee drifts.
Always step down; never jump down.
regressions: Single-leg balance and hop-and-stick on the floor.
progressions: Raise the box gradually, only while the landing stays quiet and aligned.
One-to-one box jumps (single-leg takeoff and landing) once this drill is solid.
